name: Hyundai Motor India Ltd.
business_summary: India's second-largest passenger-vehicle maker (82.5% owned by Hyundai Motor Company, Korea), listed October 2024. SUV-led portfolio (Creta, Venue, Alcazar, Exter) plus Grand i10/Aura/i20, Verna, Ioniq/Creta Electric. ~78% domestic, ~20% exports (Middle East, Africa, Latin America, South Asia; 4 million cumulative exports). Talegaon (Pune) plant inaugurated 2026-10-14 under a Rs 11,000 cr plan to 2030, lifting capacity toward 11.4 lakh units. Debt-free; pays royalty to the parent (~3.5% of sales, model knowledge). Sep-26 quarter: sales Rs 20,696 cr (record), OPM 10%, net profit Rs 1,196 cr (-24% y/y).

revenue_mix.geography: Middle East, Africa, Latin America, South Asia (model knowledge)

cost_structure.input: Royalty to Hyundai Motor Co (~3.5% of sales)

current_state.trend: Volume records but margin compression from 13% (FY25) to ~10% on commodity, FX, royalty and new-plant costs; share slide flagged; stock +6% on results as the worst looks priced in

Intensity of new-model competition in India passenger vehicles
new_nodes_proposed.ssu: +1 = major new-model wave by rivals (about -1pp share for incumbent)

exposures.mechanism: 100% passenger vehicles, ~78% domestic. +10% industry volumes with share held => revenue +8-10%; incremental contribution ~22% vs 10% Q2 OPM => EBITDA +17-22%; EV/MCap ~0.97 (debt free); persistence 0.5 => ~+9. Q2 FY27 sales were a record (Rs 20,696 cr) but margin 10% shows demand alone is not enough.

Steel ~12% of costs => 10.8% of revenue; +7% => 0.76% of revenue; at 10% OPM => EBITDA -7.6%; ~40% passed through via price hikes => -4.5%; x0.97 x0.3 => -1.3. Global HRC +20.6% since June is a live headwind.

evidence.note: Upstox: rising costs hit Q2 margins

exposures.mechanism: Aluminium ~3% of costs => 2.7% of revenue; +10% => EBITDA -2.7%; 60% unrecovered => -1.6%; x0.97x0.3 => -0.5. Aluminium -19.6% since June is a tailwind to Q3/Q4 margins.
Copper ~2% of costs; +10% => 0.18% of revenue => EBITDA -1.8%; 60% unrecovered => -1.1%; x0.97x0.3 => -0.3.
Platinum-group metals in catalytic converters ~3% of costs (model knowledge); +10% => EBITDA -2.7%; mostly recovered via pass-through over 2 quarters => -0.4.

Plastics/petrochemicals ~6% of costs (+10% Brent => ~+4% resin => ~0.2% of revenue) plus higher running cost lowers demand for petrol/diesel PVs. EBITDA -2% from cost, -1% from demand; x0.97 x0.3-0.5 => ~-1. Empirical -0.74 (t=-1.3) agrees on sign.

Exports ~20% of volumes (USD/other) vs imported parts/CKD ~15-20% of revenue plus royalty to parent (~3.5%, model knowledge, linked to USD/KRW): near-neutral net. +3% INR depreciation => +0.6% of revenue from exports, -0.6% from imports/royalty. Empirical +2.42 (t=1.6) suggests a modest positive; sign uncertain.

evidence.note: Export and import shares are estimates

exposures.mechanism: ~80% of PVs are financed; +25bp repo => EMI +0.5% => volume -0.7% (assumption) => EBITDA -1.5%; x0.97 x0.5 => -0.7. RBI hiked 25bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026 and says cuts are off the table near term.
P/E 37.8: +25bp on cost of equity => ~-2% pure DCF; cash-rich so tempered.

Further broad GST cut (+1 = 2-5pp price cut): ~3% price reduction x elasticity 1.2 => volumes +3.6% => EBITDA +8.8% (22% incremental margin on 10% OPM); policy is structural (1.0) but Hyundai's share of any boost is ~13% market share-weighted and the Sept-2025 cut is already in the base => +5. Event risk is on the upside only if the government acts again.

New-model waves from Maruti, Tata, Mahindra, Kia, Toyota in the compact SUV segment erode Hyundai's share (market-share slide flagged by Moneycontrol 2026-09-23; Jefferies caution 2026-10-29). +1 (strong wave) => -1pp share ~ -8% volume => EBITDA -18% x0.97 x0.25 persistence ~-4; reduced to -3 given Bayon/new Venue response.

Chip/rare-earth shortages halt lines; +1 => ~-2% annual volume, operating leverage 22% on 10% OPM => EBITDA -4.4%; x0.97 x0.5 => -2.1, rounded -2.5. Hyundai Motor Group supply chain relies on Korea/China electronics.

Exports (~20% of volumes) go to the Middle East, Africa and Latin America; Gulf escalation disrupts shipping and demand and lifts oil. +1 => export volumes -10% => revenue -2% => EBITDA -4% x0.97 x0.3 => -1.2. Brent hit $100+ on 8 Oct 2026 on Hormuz risk.
SUV-led mix (Creta, Alcazar, Venue) lifts ASP; EV and hybrid (Pune plant plans hybrid production, RushLane 2026-10-14). +1 => +1% ASP at full drop-through => EBITDA +10% x0.97 x0.2 => ~+2.

FII holding fell from 5.43% (Mar) to 3.19% (Sep 2026) after the IPO lock-in period; DIIs absorbed (11.85%). +US$5bn quarterly inflow => ~+1.5% for a stock with 3% FII ownership and beta 1.2; moves are flow-driven, not fundamental.
